finding.text: There are now two root assistants: Layers.js makes `assistant-root` for page `/` on Opus (diff.patch:992), while Global.js still spawns `master-assistant`. The owner's page-less prompts no longer reach `master-assistant` (Global.js `heard()` dropped the prompt line, diff.patch:597), so the part of deliverable 3 that says "the root assistant hears the owner's page-less prompts" only holds for `assistant-root`. Pick one of the two: make `/` resolve to `master-assistant`, or retire Global's copy.

The landings and blocks of the root's direct children never reach the root that hears prompts. `Global.direct_child()` (diff.patch:591) only counts agents whose parent is `dispatcher`, `mastermind-servex` or `master-assistant`. But a card's manager is spawned with `parent: rec.assistant.id` (Layers.js spec, diff.patch:1003), so its landings are dropped, and `assistant-root` hears no landings at all.

Deliverable 1 says a child pair "is spawned by" its parent page's mastermind. The code only writes `parent` into layers.json (diff.patch:786). The agents themselves are still spawned by Layers, and a manager's runtime parent is its own assistant. So the policy "tree" rule from deliverable 4 does not connect `manager-<card>` to `manager-root`, and the parent↔child messaging proved in roles/proof.md only covers two `task-mastermind-*` ids, not a real page pair.

Deliverable 2 asks for one assistant text, but there are two copies of it, and they already disagree. The copy that is actually loaded is `Servex/agents/card-assistant.md` (Layers passes `setting_sources: []`, so no skill loads). It says "you have no file-read tool" (diff.patch:1478), yet the same spec gives the assistant Read/Edit/Write/Bash (diff.patch:984). `.claude/skills/every-prompt/page-assistant.md` is a second copy that nothing loads. Keep one file and have Layers read that one.

`External.register()` (diff.patch:281) overwrites any registry row, including a real agent's. If `register_session({id: "assistant-foo"})` is called, then while `assistant-foo` is stopped, `Agents.send()` (diff.patch:206) sends to an inbox instead of waking the agent. It should refuse an id that already belongs to a non-external agent.

policy.js gives a registered external id the owner's full reach, including "spawn anything" (diff.patch:2271, 2280). Anything that can call `register_session` gets that reach, which is more than deliverable 8 asked for. Consider letting it only message.

The two skills disagree on the inbox Monitor. The `page-assistant.md` section says "no expiry, `until: never`" (diff.patch:99), but the servex-mastermind SKILL.md section says a Monitor lasts 30 minutes at most (diff.patch:141). The requirement asks for no expiry, so say which is true in both places.

A plain page's chat goes to `public<page>ai/chat.jsonl` (Layers.js `chat_file`, diff.patch:849). For `/framework/` that path lands inside the task-log dir `public/framework/ai/`, and every page gets an `ai/` folder inside the live-reloaded tree. A path under Servex's home would avoid both problems.

The quick-edit rules from deliverable 5 ("only inside your own directory, no claim covers it") are enforced by prompt text alone (diff.patch:1506–1525). Nothing in code checks the edited paths against the scope or the claims before `merge.mjs` runs.

The ids are `manager-<page>`, but the requirement names the pair `mastermind-<page>` (roles.js keeps `manager` as an alias, diff.patch:2386). That is fine as a naming decision, but the landing should say so outright rather than tick deliverable 1 as written.

The lifecycle work looks sound and is well proved in pairs/proof.md: created on first use, stopped after 5 idle minutes, at most 4 live, resume or fresh, and a checkpoint instead of compaction. The inbox also delivered within 2 seconds (inbox/proof.md:59, 5 ms). No change needed there.

The root assistant is told to read deeper pages on demand with `list_cards` and `list_agents` (Servex/agents/master-assistant.md:1-7), but Global.js:637 gives it only card_reply, send_to_agent, list_claims, page_reply and ask_manager, and `disallowedTools` hides every other Servex tool. So deliverable 3's "everything else it reads on demand" cannot happen. Add those two tools to `master_tools`.

Your own proof fails on the owner's lifecycle bar: "one recycled assistant whose context begins under 10k" shows `FAIL ... 10867` (pairs/proof.txt:40), and page-pairs.md says a fresh assistant starts at about 11k. Either trim the start (for example, move the "If you are a VS Code tab" section out of page-assistant.md:165-175, since every spawned assistant carries it in its system prompt) and re-run the proof, or say plainly in the landing that this item missed.

`register_session` checks only that `id` is a string (External.js:344), and then `file(id)` puts it straight into a path (External.js:368). An id like `../../x` writes outside `logs/inbox/`. Accept only `/^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*$/`.

Deliverable 8's "Watch" asks for lines in the `every-prompt` skill. They went into every-prompt/page-assistant.md:165, which a front-desk tab loads only "if you are a page's own assistant" (SKILL.md:18). So the tab that needs them never reads them. Put the lines in SKILL.md itself, or add a "Load this if… you are a VS Code tab" link there.

roles.js:784 folds `master-assistant` into the `page-assistant` row. A plain `spawn_agent({role: "master-assistant"})` now gets the fast model and `bypassPermissions` where it used to get the architect tier and `plan`. Global.js is unaffected because it passes its own fields, but the alias quietly loosens the posture for any other caller.

Deliverable 1 asks for ids named `mastermind-<page>`, and for a child pair to be spawned by its parent's mastermind. The ids are `manager-<page>`, and a pair is started by the first prompt with its assistant as the live parent (Layers.js:1156; the tree link lives only in layers.json). page-pairs.md:1951 admits the naming. The owner should hear about both gaps in the landing, not only in a doc.

Deliverable 2 says the root assistant loads the same one skill as every page assistant. The root instead reads its own master-assistant.md (Layers.js:825, page-assistant.md:36-38). That is defensible, but it is a second text to keep true.

Deliverable 5's rules ("only your own directory, only unclaimed files") exist only as prompt text. The assistant runs with Bash and `bypassPermissions` (Layers.js:1136-1145), and nothing checks the paths before merge.mjs. page-pairs.md:1948 already lists this. Even one path check in merge.mjs, run against the scope, would make the rule real.

A plain page's chat is written to `public/<page>/ai/chat.jsonl` (Layers.js:1000), inside the live-reloaded site tree, and the root's chat lands at `public/ai/`. Check that the watcher ignores these files, or each reply may reload the page the owner is talking on. A path under Servex's home would be simpler.

Deliverable 6's fresh-restart threshold skips the root: `master-assistant` is excluded from `sweep()` (Layers.js:1450), and Global only recycles it once a day. On a busy day the Opus root can grow past 40k with no checkpoint.
`Policy.kind()` reads registry.json from disk on every message check (policy.js:2579-2581) via `registered_external`. That is cheap today, but it is a synchronous file read on every `send_to_agent`.
